verdict.rationale: DBOS documents queues that run many workflows at once with managed concurrency, and `DBOS.start_workflow` for background launches. That gives queue-based triggering and a form of fan-out, but triggering is imperative code calls rather than declarative event or webhook bindings. A community report of a Kafka-consumer pipeline that ran exactly-once per message adds some corroboration for event-driven use. Missing for 10: declarative event/webhook trigger bindings, documented first-party event-source integrations (e.g. Kafka), explicit one-event-to-many-functions fan-out docs, independent hands-on corroboration of fan-out.

support.subject: As a backend developer, events from my app, webhooks, or queues trigger workflows declaratively, and one event can fan out to many functions

citations.quote: You can use queues to run many workflows at once with managed concurrency.
You can use DBOS.start_workflow to start a workflow in the background.
a Kafka-consumer customer used DBOS to build an event processing pipeline that ran exactly-once per Kafka message
